title: fix(github): detect signatures by standalone marker, not body text
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Task

Make every GitHub signing layer recognize an existing signature only from the canonical marker on its own line. A body that merely references the root `aidevops.sh` filename or discusses the marker inline must still receive a signature, while a body carrying a standalone marker line must receive no second footer.

## Why

`gh-signature-helper.sh:415-417` currently treats any occurrence of the text `aidevops.sh` as proof that the body is signed. Framework issue bodies routinely cite `aidevops.sh:line`, so this false positive suppresses the audit footer on create or body-edit paths. Conversely, a body carrying a standalone canonical marker but no visible link text receives another footer. Wrapper and shim predicates also use unanchored marker-substring checks, so inline documentation of the marker can be mistaken for a completed footer.

This was observed while enriching issue `#29040`: a signed issue body was replaced through the safe body-file edit path with content that cited `aidevops.sh:1715`; the resulting GitHub body had no standalone signature marker. The footer then had to be generated canonically and applied in a second edit.

## Reproducer

- **Symptom command**: `bash .agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh footer --body "See aidevops.sh:1715 for the release entry point" | wc -c`
- **Actual output**: `0`, so an unsigned body receives no footer solely because it mentions the root script filename.
- **Expected output**: A non-zero canonical footer containing one standalone signature-marker line.
- **Control command**: `python3 -c 'import subprocess; p=subprocess.run(["bash", ".agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh", "footer", "--body", "Existing footer\n<\x21-- aidevops:sig -->\n---\nsigned"], capture_output=True); print(len(p.stdout))'`
- **Control output**: `223`, so a body with an existing standalone marker line incorrectly receives another footer when visible link text is absent.
- **Causal status**: confirmed.
- **Production entry point**: `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh:399-425` implements body deduplication for generated footers.
- **Call chain**: `.agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh:440-452`, `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-session.sh:415-463`, and `.agents/scripts/gh:2305-2353` call the helper while preparing GitHub bodies.
- **Integrated verification**: Issue `#29040` changed from `hasSignature=true` after creation to `hasSignature=false` after a safe body edit containing `aidevops.sh` references, then returned to `hasSignature=true` only after a canonical footer was explicitly added.

## What

1. Replace filename and unanchored-substring deduplication with standalone canonical-marker-line detection across helper, wrapper, and shim paths.
2. Add direct helper regression tests for root-filename, inline-marker, and existing-footer cases.
3. Add an integrated wrapper or shim fixture proving a body-file edit containing an `aidevops.sh` path publishes exactly one standalone marker line.
4. Preserve existing signature format, metadata auto-detection, and fail-open transport behavior.

## Session Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-31
- **Runtime:** OpenCode interactive session
- **Context:** Discovered while filing and enriching worker-ready release-provenance issue `#29040`.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall completed for signature deduplication and body-file edits; zero reusable hits.
- [x] Open and historical GitHub issue/PR searches found no task for this exact marker-versus-filename defect.
- [x] Prior merged PR `#19102` established signature enforcement but does not cover this false-dedup condition.
- [x] Current `origin/main` at `dfb6bc4a5b76af8697a299b3a17fc74b7c7fecdb` still contains the filename-substring check.
- [x] Named implementation and test files were verified as tracked.
- [x] Workload tier is `standard`: the fix is localized, but integrated audit-trail regression coverage is required.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped because a worker-ready issue plus exact reproducer is sufficient.

## Worker Quick-Start

1. Read `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh:395-425` and compare its dedup predicate with marker checks in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-session.sh:415-444` and `.agents/scripts/gh:2305-2353`.
2. Add the two direct failing fixtures before changing production code.
3. Use the canonical HTML marker on its own line as the sole idempotency key; neither visible link text nor an inline marker mention proves a footer exists.
4. Add one integrated body-file fixture that contains an `aidevops.sh` file reference and assert exactly one standalone marker line reaches the captured GitHub body.

## How

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh` — use standalone marker-line detection for `--body` deduplication.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-session.sh` — align body and body-file predicates with standalone marker-line semantics.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh` — align shim body and body-file predicates with standalone marker-line semantics.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-signature-helper.sh` — direct false-positive, false-negative, and existing-footer tests.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` — body-file wrapper regression with a root-script reference.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh` — only if the most representative edit-path capture belongs in shim integration coverage.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh:440-452`, `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-session.sh:381-467`, and `.agents/scripts/gh:2206-2353` consume footer output and deduplicate body signatures.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh:679-734`, `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:256-288`, and `.agents/scripts/gh:2383-2387` publish issue, PR, comment, and edit bodies after signature preparation.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-signature-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-edit-safety.sh` cover helper, wrapper, shim, and safe-edit behavior.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh:423-425` defines the canonical HTML marker inline; no external schema or configuration file exists.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys repository `.agents/scripts/` to runtime bundles; edit repository sources only and leave deployed copies untouched.
- **Migrations/backfills:** Not applicable because `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh` changes future footer generation only; existing unsigned bodies are not automatically rewritten, as confirmed by the caller search.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-session.sh:431-463` and `.agents/scripts/gh:2320-2353` own temporary signed-body cleanup; rollback is the localized predicate revert with no persistent-state conversion.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add or reuse a line-aware predicate that recognizes the canonical marker only when it occupies a complete line, then apply equivalent semantics in helper, wrapper, and shim paths.
2. Add direct tests proving root-script and inline-marker prose emit one footer while an existing standalone marker emits zero additional bytes.
3. Add integrated body-file coverage proving a GitHub edit payload with an `aidevops.sh` path retains exactly one standalone marker line.
4. Run focused tests and changed-file lint; keep metadata formatting and fallback behavior unchanged.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Footer generation is a pure per-invocation transformation; preserve temporary-copy behavior so concurrent GitHub writes never mutate caller-owned body files.
- **Migration/rollback:** No stored schema changes; old unsigned bodies remain untouched and rollback only restores the prior predicate.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Signature text and CLI options remain unchanged, so older callers continue to work while updated runtimes correct deduplication.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Standalone marker-line detection guarantees repeated signing attempts produce at most one canonical footer while inline documentation remains signable.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Keep current fail-open behavior when metadata generation fails; this fix changes only the dedup decision, not transport retries or fallback routing.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-signature-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-edit-safety.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** Signature-helper tests prove standalone-marker semantics; wrapper and shim tests prove body-file publication contains one footer; safe-edit tests protect validated edit transport; changed-file lint covers shell quality.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required because the change is localized marker recognition with focused helper, wrapper, shim, and safe-edit coverage and no schema or dependency change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-session.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-signature-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An unsigned body containing an `aidevops.sh` filename reference receives one canonical signature footer.
- [ ] A body with a standalone signature-marker line does not receive another footer, even when visible link text is absent.
- [ ] An inline marker mention does not count as a completed signature and still receives a footer.
- [ ] Integrated body-file signing publishes exactly one standalone marker line and preserves the caller-owned source file.
- [ ] Signature format, metadata fields, CLI compatibility, and fail-open behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused tests and changed-file lint pass.

## Context & Decisions

- The canonical HTML marker is already the identity signal, but every layer must require it as a complete line so inline documentation cannot suppress signing.
- Visible `aidevops.sh` text is legitimate implementation context and cannot prove a footer exists.
- Do not backfill or edit existing public bodies as part of this task.
- Do not weaken signature requirements or suppress metadata generation.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh:399-425` — defective dedup predicate and canonical marker output.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-session.sh:415-463` — unanchored wrapper marker checks to align.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:2305-2353` — unanchored body and body-file shim marker checks to align.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-signature-helper.sh` — direct helper test pattern.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` — wrapper body-file capture pattern.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** None; current-origin code and exact command output confirm the defect.
- **Blocks:** Reliable audit signatures on framework issue bodies and edits that cite the root script.
- **External:** No credentials, purchases, API changes, or public-body backfill required.

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Tests first | 15m | Direct and integrated failing fixtures |
| Implementation | 15m | Align standalone-marker predicates across three paths |

title: bug(pulse-merge): _pulse_merge_preflight_snapshot_gate has 7 silent failure paths — approved+clean PRs stuck with eligible_unmerged=0, no audit trail
body:
## Description

`_pulse_merge_preflight_snapshot_gate` (`pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:968`) has 7 of 9 failure paths that return 1 with no `LOGFILE` entry — only two paths produce log output (line 995 "head changed" and line 1036 success). When any of the silent paths fire, the PR is skipped every merge cycle with `merged=0, failed=0, eligible_unmerged=0` and no audit trail.

This creates a second problem: `_pmp_record_processed_pr_result` only increments `eligible_unmerged` on result code 3, but `_process_single_ready_pr` returns 1 (not 3) when `_pulse_merge_final_trust_gate` fails. So the monitoring counter stays 0 even when approved+clean PRs are blocked every cycle.

Observed effect: 4 APPROVED+CLEAN PRs in Majowka/mesh-manager (#3427, #3424, #3433, #3434) have been stuck for multiple hours. All upstream gate checks log success (worker-briefed, review-bot, required-checks, ruleset 1/1) but `pre-merge snapshot: ... verified` never appears in the log for any of them, while it does appear for repos where merges succeed (Majowka/.github, Majowka/aidevops-routines).

## Expected Behavior

Every failure path in `_pulse_merge_preflight_snapshot_gate` should emit a `LOGFILE` entry naming the blocker reason and PR, matching the pattern already used for "head changed" and "unresolved review thread(s)".

`_process_single_ready_pr` should return 3 (not 1) when the preflight snapshot gate blocks a PR that passed all earlier gate checks, so `eligible_unmerged` is incremented and monitoring sees the stuck PRs.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `grep "pre-merge snapshot" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep "mesh-manager"`

**Actual output**: empty — no snapshot log at all for Majowka/mesh-manager PRs despite them passing all earlier gate checks.

**Expected output**:
```
[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: current head <sha>, fresh review gate, ... verified for PR #3427
```
OR a specific blocker line such as:
```
[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE (activity fetch failed) for PR #3427 in Majowka/mesh-manager
```

**Contrast** (repos where merges succeed):
```
[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: current head 7009bf657d62, fresh review gate, ... verified for PR #160 in Majowka/.github (GH#27137)
[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: current head b6b24ced3b90, ... verified for PR #41 in Majowka/aidevops-routines (GH#27137)
```

**Gate checks that DO log success (visible in pulse.log)**:
```
[pulse-merge] worker-briefed auto-merge: PR #3427 passed all gates (issue #3329, ...)
[pulse-wrapper] Review bot gate: PASS for PR #3427 (typed current-head evidence)
[pulse-merge] _check_required_checks_has_terminal_failure: no terminal failed required contexts for PR #3427
[pulse-wrapper] approve_collaborator_pr: PR #3427 already has trusted approval from kamcio2603
[pulse-merge] _check_ruleset_required_reviews_passing: PR #3427 satisfies 1/1 ruleset-required approval(s)
```

Immediately after these, the pass moves to the next repo with no merge attempt and no snapshot log.

**Pass timing evidence** (every cycle, `pulse.log`):
```
deterministic_merge_pass timing: repo=Majowka/mesh-manager total_s=276 merged=0 closed=0 failed=0 prs=11
Deterministic merge pass complete: merged=0, closed_conflicting=0, failed=0, eligible_unmerged=0
```

`eligible_unmerged=0` despite APPROVED+CLEAN PRs passing all upstream gate checks.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:
- **Production entry point**: `pulse-merge-process.sh:430` -- `_process_single_ready_pr "$repo_slug" "$pr_obj"` called after all upstream checks pass
- **Call chain**: `_merge_ready_prs_for_repo` -> `_process_single_ready_pr:1534` -> `_pulse_merge_final_trust_gate` -> `_pulse_merge_preflight_snapshot_gate:968` -> one of 7 silent `return 1` paths -> `_process_single_ready_pr` returns 1 -> `_pmp_record_processed_pr_result` rc=1 -> no counter incremented
- **Integrated verification**: confirmed by absence of `pre-merge snapshot: ... verified` for any mesh-manager PR across 15+ merge cycles in `pulse.log`

**Causal code** -- silent failure paths in `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:968`:

```bash
# Line 977-980: PR fetch failure -- NO LOG
pr_json=$(_pmrc_gh_read gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/pulls/${pr_number}" 2>/dev/null) || {
    _PULSE_MERGE_PREFLIGHT_BLOCKER_KIND="$PMRC_BLOCKER_SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE"
    _pmrc_snapshot_log_failure ...   # <- logs to a different location, NOT to LOGFILE
    return 1
}
# Line 998-1001: required-context lookup -- NO LOGFILE ENTRY
# Line 1003-1005: checks_json fetch -- NO LOGFILE ENTRY
# Line 1010-1012: activity_json fetch -- NO LOGFILE ENTRY
# Line 1015-1017: review gate freshness -- NO LOGFILE ENTRY
# Line 1024-1030: checks acceptable -- NO LOGFILE ENTRY
# Line 1032-1034: quiet period -- NO LOGFILE ENTRY
```

Only two paths do write to LOGFILE:
- Line 995: head SHA changed (explicit echo to LOGFILE)
- Line 1036: success (explicit echo to LOGFILE)

**Call-site sweep** for `_pulse_merge_preflight_snapshot_gate` in `pulse-merge.sh`:
- Line 562: inside `_pulse_merge_final_trust_gate` (called at lines 1534 and 1564 of `_process_single_ready_pr`)
- Line 1486: dry-run path (not relevant)

**Counter gap** in `pulse-merge-process.sh:310`:

```bash
_pmp_record_processed_pr_result() {
    case "$result_code" in
    0) merged++   ;;
    2) closed++   ;;
    3) failed++; outcome="eligible-unmerged"  # <- ONLY this increments eligible_unmerged
    4) outcome="deferred"                      # <- native auto-merge
    # rc=1 has no case -- no counter, outcome="blocked"
    esac
}
```

`_process_single_ready_pr` returns 1 (not 3) for final-trust-gate failures (lines 1541, 1566 of `pulse-merge.sh`), so `eligible_unmerged` stays 0.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an APPROVED+CLEAN worker PR in a repo where `_pulse_merge_preflight_snapshot_gate` silently fails
2. Run merge pass
3. Observe: all upstream gate checks log success, but no `pre-merge snapshot` line appears for that PR
4. Observe: `merged=0, failed=0, eligible_unmerged=0` in timing summary

## Proposed Fix

**Bug A (observability)**: add `echo "[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: <BLOCKER_REASON> for PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug}" >>"$LOGFILE"` before every `return 1` in `_pulse_merge_preflight_snapshot_gate`, using the already-set `_PULSE_MERGE_PREFLIGHT_BLOCKER_KIND` value as the reason string.

**Bug B (counter)**: in `_process_single_ready_pr` (pulse-merge.sh:1534-1541 and 1564-1567), return 3 instead of 1 when `_pulse_merge_final_trust_gate` fails for a PR that passed all upstream gate checks. This distinguishes "upstream gate blocked" (rc=1, correct) from "preflight snapshot blocked a merge-ready PR" (rc=3, eligible_unmerged++).

## Workarounds Applied

None needed for diagnosis -- issue was found via absence-of-evidence pattern (no `pre-merge snapshot: ... verified` for mesh-manager). For unblocking the specific stuck PRs: manually run `gh pr merge N --repo Majowka/mesh-manager --squash --admin` if appropriate.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.200
- **Latest version**: 3.32.200
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

- Observed repo: Majowka/mesh-manager -- 11 open PRs, 4 APPROVED+CLEAN (#3427/#3329, #3424/#3352, #3433/#3354, #3434/#3404)
- Most likely blocker candidate: `PMRC_BLOCKER_SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE` from `_pmrc_snapshot_bot_activity_json` (line 1010) timing out on large PR comment threads (mesh-manager PRs have CodeRabbit rate-limit comments + multiple worker comments), or `PMRC_BLOCKER_REVIEW_GATE` from `_pmrc_snapshot_review_gate_fresh` failing on stale evidence at the second `_pulse_merge_final_trust_gate` call (line 1564 of pulse-merge.sh, which runs after `_set_native_auto_merge_or_skip`)
- Related: GH#29024 (CHANGES_REQUESTED remediation-first closes PR on dedup) -- same session, same repo
- `_pmrc_snapshot_log_failure` (called on some paths) writes to a diagnostic file, NOT to `LOGFILE`, so it does not appear in `pulse.log`

title: bug(pulse-dispatch-lib): _dispatch_recent_dirty_worktree_marker_active passes comments JSON as env var — E2BIG on issues with 50+ comments, dirty-worktree check silently bypassed
body:
## Description

`_dispatch_recent_dirty_worktree_marker_active` in `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:408` passes the full GitHub issues comments JSON as an environment variable (`AIDEVOPS_DIRTY_WORKTREE_COMMENTS_JSON`) to a `python3` subprocess. When an issue has many comments (e.g., 50+), the JSON payload exceeds the Linux kernel `ARG_MAX` limit (~2MB combined argv+envp), causing `E2BIG: Argument list too long` on every pulse cycle that evaluates such an issue.

The error is swallowed by `|| marker_state=""` (line 476), so dispatch continues with the dirty-worktree check silently bypassed — but the error line is emitted to pulse.log every cycle, producing persistent noise and obscuring real failures.

## Expected Behavior

The comments JSON should be passed via a temporary file (or process substitution) rather than an environment variable, eliminating the `ARG_MAX` ceiling entirely.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: any pulse dispatch cycle evaluating an issue with 50+ comments

**Actual output** (extracted from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, appears every ~2 minutes across multiple aidevops versions):

```
~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.32.199-.../agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh: line 432: /bin/python3: Argument list too long
~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.32.200-.../agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh: line 476: /bin/python3: Argument list too long
```

Observed at log lines: 133681, 134102, 134961, 135197, 135648, 136124, 136682, 137232, 137571, 138029, 138090 (10+ occurrences across versions 3.32.199 and 3.32.200 in a single session).

Triggered by issues with large comment threads, e.g., `<managed-repo>#3351` (`comments=52`, noted in log as "clean-room brief mode for comment-bloated issue comments=52 ops=51 chars=23476").

**Expected output**: no error line; `_dispatch_recent_dirty_worktree_marker_active` runs cleanly and returns the correct marker state.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:
- **Production entry point**: `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:408` -- `_dispatch_recent_dirty_worktree_marker_active` called during dispatch preflight for each candidate issue
- **Call chain**: `dispatch_with_dedup` -> `_dispatch_recent_dirty_worktree_marker_active:394` -> `comments_json=$(gh api ...)` -> `AIDEVOPS_DIRTY_WORKTREE_COMMENTS_JSON="$comments_json" python3 - ... <<'PY'` -> kernel exec() with oversized envp -> E2BIG -> `|| marker_state=""` swallows error
- **Integrated verification**: reproduce by calling `_dispatch_recent_dirty_worktree_marker_active` on any issue with 50+ comments where the combined JSON size exceeds ~1.5MB

**Causal code** (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:404-408`):

```bash
comments_json=$(gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/issues/${issue_number}/comments?per_page=100" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
[[ -n "$comments_json" ]] || return 1

local marker_state=""
marker_state=$(AIDEVOPS_DIRTY_WORKTREE_COMMENTS_JSON="$comments_json" python3 - "$hold_seconds" ... <<'PY'
# Python reads: json.loads(os.environ.get("AIDEVOPS_DIRTY_WORKTREE_COMMENTS_JSON", ""))
```

The env var approach hits `ARG_MAX` because Linux counts all environment variable bytes against the exec limit. A JSON array of 52 comments averages ~450 bytes/comment = ~23KB, which is safely under the limit on its own — but combined with all other inherited environment variables (PATH, pulse config vars, etc.), the total envp can exceed 2MB on active pulse workers.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an issue with 50+ comments in a managed repo
2. Pulse dispatch cycle runs `_dispatch_recent_dirty_worktree_marker_active` for that issue
3. Observe `Argument list too long` in `pulse.log` at the `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` line

## Proposed Fix

Replace the env-var pass with a tempfile approach:

```bash
local _dwt_tmp
_dwt_tmp=$(mktemp) || return 1
printf '%s' "$comments_json" > "$_dwt_tmp"
marker_state=$(python3 - "$hold_seconds" "${AIDEVOPS_DIRTY_WORKTREE_NOW_EPOCH:-}" "$_dwt_tmp" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys
hold_seconds = int(sys.argv[1])
now_override = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ""
comments_file = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else ""
try:
    comments = json.loads(open(comments_file).read()) if comments_file else []
except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
    print("clear"); sys.exit(0)
# ... rest of script unchanged ...
PY
)
rm -f "$_dwt_tmp"
```

This eliminates the `ARG_MAX` ceiling entirely since file paths are short regardless of content size.

## Workarounds Applied

None — the `|| marker_state=""` fallback means dispatch continues safely (fail-open), but the dirty-worktree check is silently bypassed for comment-heavy issues, which could theoretically allow re-dispatch of a dirty-worktree issue before recovery.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.200
- **Latest version**: 3.32.200
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

- Error present across multiple runtime bundle versions (3.32.199 and 3.32.200) — not a regression, pre-existing
- `per_page=100` cap limits worst case to ~100 comments, but even at ~230 bytes/comment average the total can approach limits when combined with inherited envp from pulse workers
- Same pattern risk exists anywhere else in the codebase that passes large API responses as environment variables to subprocess invocations
- Related session: GH#29024, GH#29043 (same diagnostic session, `<managed-repo>`)

title: Fix social persistence clock forwarding and batch provenance
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `Slack knowledge ingestion clock forwarding reconciliation` returned no reusable lesson.
- [x] Discovery pass: no matching issue or open/merged PR was found for production social-clock forwarding or lease `now_epoch` revalidation; recent target-file history was inspected.
- [x] File refs verified: the lease, provider-neutral persistence, reconciliation, and focused sync-test paths exist on fetched `origin/main` at `4831ff72d`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` because the fix coordinates lease fencing, transaction timestamps, canonical batch provenance, reconciliation, and production/test clock boundaries across four files.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped because the implementation will proceed immediately in an interactive linked worktree after issue creation.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-31
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session
- **Parent task:** #28659
- **Blocks:** #28782 through a GitHub native relationship.
- **Conversation context:** Slack collector verification exposed two provider-neutral defects that cannot be repaired in provider issue #28782: production callers re-submit a real clock value through a test-only override boundary, and normalized rows reference a raw batch ID that differs from the persisted fetch-batch primary key.

## What

Repair provider-neutral social persistence so an internally sampled production clock can be reused safely inside one fenced transaction without becoming a public deterministic-clock override. Store the content-addressed raw envelope ID as the fetch-batch primary key, retain the response-body digest in `response_hash`, and restore complete reconciliation inventory/provenance behavior.

## Why

On current `main`, `renew_run_lease()` and `update_run_receipt()` sample `social_now()` and then pass that integer back through `assert_run_lease(..., now_epoch=...)`; `social_now(explicit)` correctly rejects explicit values outside `AIDEVOPS_TEST_MODE=1`. Real collectors therefore fail after acquiring a lease. Separately, `_insert_fetch_batch()` imports objects/activities with `raw.batch_id` but inserts `raw.response_hash` as `fetch_batches.batch_id`, so reconciliation cannot join canonical rows to their connection/stream. The focused sync suite currently reports 28 passes and five reconciliation failures, including zero missing/present inventory.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** Four shared files, a security-sensitive test-only clock seam, fencing semantics, and canonical evidence identity require design and regression judgment rather than a mechanical edit.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** The active interactive session has the exact failing evidence and will implement and verify the repair immediately.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** fetched `origin/main` at `4831ff72d`; target files and current failures were inspected on 2026-07-31.
- **Verification run:** `bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh` → 28 passed, 5 failed on current behavior.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** re-read the four target files after creating the linked worktree; stop if another PR changes clock validation, fetch-batch identity, or reconciliation inventory first.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_lease.py:74-95,230-398` and `.agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_collect_persist.py:98-149,255-305` for the clock trust boundary and batch mapping.
- **Then read:** `.agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_reconcile.py:152-201,348-395` and `.agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh:72-82,311-454,484-588` for inventory and expiry regressions.
- **Stop when:** one validated wall-clock sample is reused only through private/internal helpers, public explicit overrides remain test-only, row batch IDs join fetch batches, and the focused suite is fully green.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_lease.py:254-398` — separate public clock validation from internal already-validated timestamp fencing/receipt operations.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_collect_persist.py:21-27,125-149,255-305,363-475` — use internal validated-clock helpers and correct fetch-batch field mapping.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_reconcile.py:18-24,348-395` — reuse its single validated timestamp without reopening the override seam.
- `EDIT: .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh:72-82,311-454,484-588` — prove production no-override lifecycle behavior, expiry rollback, canonical batch joins, and reconciliation.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_knowledge_social_collect_persist.py`, `_knowledge_social_reconcile.py`, and provider collectors call lease fencing and receipt updates; queries/reconciliation join normalized `batch_id` values to `fetch_batches`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `_knowledge_social_lease.py` updates `collector_leases`/`sync_runs`; `_knowledge_social_collect_persist.py` writes raw envelopes, normalized rows, fetch batches, coverage, and cursors; reconciliation writes evidence and missing/present state.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh` exercises production/test clocks, stale fences, transaction rollback, batch provenance, and reconciliation; existing X fixtures seed canonical rows.
- **Schemas/config:** no schema or configuration change; preserve schema version 5 and `AIDEVOPS_TEST_MODE` as the only explicit-clock authorization.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** scripts deploy through `setup.sh`; no generated source or credential material changes.
- **Migrations/backfills:** no migration; existing malformed fetch-batch provenance is test/development evidence and this fix must not rewrite user corpora speculatively.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** transaction rollback in `_knowledge_social_collect_persist.py` and exact release in `_knowledge_social_lease.py` remain unchanged; reverting the commit restores prior behavior without data deletion.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add private/internal lease and receipt helpers that accept an already validated integer timestamp. Keep public `now_epoch` APIs routed through `social_now()` so external production overrides still fail closed.
2. Route `renew_run_lease()`, provider-neutral page/terminal/stop persistence, and reconciliation through the internal helpers after sampling/validating their clock once per decision point. Preserve the two-sample expiry regression where persistence must fail if the lease expires before receipt commit.
3. Change `_insert_fetch_batch()` so `batch_id=raw.batch_id` and `response_hash=raw.response_hash`; keep request hash, blob reference, and terminal metadata unchanged.
4. Add a production-mode regression with `AIDEVOPS_TEST_MODE` and `AIDEVOPS_SOCIAL_NOW_EPOCH` absent, plus a direct assertion that normalized rows reference an existing fetch batch. Run focused and changed-file gates.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** never weaken identity/fencing checks; the same validated timestamp must govern each individual fence/receipt operation, while the existing expiry test must still reject a lease that expires between persistence stages.
- **Migration/rollback:** no schema or destructive rewrite; historical rows are left untouched and new writes use the corrected provenance mapping.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** public function signatures and explicit-clock test behavior remain stable; new internal helpers are private to shared modules.
- **Idempotency/retry:** content-addressed raw batch IDs remain deterministic, and `ON CONFLICT(batch_id) DO NOTHING` continues to make exact page replay idempotent.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** stale/expired fences roll back normalized rows, fetch batches, coverage, cursors, and receipts exactly as before.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash

  .agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_lease.py \
  .agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_collect_persist.py \
  .agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_reconcile.py
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh
shellcheck .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- Compilation covers the three shared Python modules.
- The focused suite must improve from 28/5 to all passing while retaining clock-override and expiry rejection.
- ShellCheck and changed-file lint cover the modified test and repository policy.
- **Surface mapping:** compilation covers the shared Python write paths; the focused suite proves production/test clock separation, lease expiry rollback, canonical batch joins, and reconciliation; ShellCheck and changed-file lint protect shell portability and repository policy.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused sync tests pass with production-clock and batch-provenance regressions.
- [ ] Create a WIP commit before broader changed-file lint.
- [ ] Rebase #28782 onto the merged repair and rerun its Slack-focused suite.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_lease.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_collect_persist.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_knowledge_social_reconcile.py`
- `.agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Real-clock lease renewal, fenced page/terminal/stop persistence, reconciliation, and receipt completion succeed with all deterministic clock environment variables absent.
- [ ] Explicit `now_epoch` and environment clock overrides remain rejected outside `AIDEVOPS_TEST_MODE=1`.
- [ ] Normalized object/activity `batch_id` values resolve to the matching `fetch_batches.batch_id`, whose `response_hash` remains the response-body digest.
- [ ] Complete, reappearing, and exact-replay reconciliation assertions pass without advancing provider cursors or weakening stale/conflict rejection.
- [ ] Expiring or stale leases still roll back every durable database path.
- [ ] No provider-specific files, schema migrations, credentials, or historical backfills are added.

## Dependencies

- **Blocks:** #28782, which must remain provider-scoped and cannot carry these shared repairs.
- **Related:** #28867 owns final provider-neutral registration and capability-matrix integration but is blocked by #28782, so this prerequisite must land separately to avoid a dependency cycle.

title: bug(pulse-triage): _triage_mark_infrastructure_retry has no cooldown — github-comments-snapshot-too-large retried every cycle indefinitely
body:
## Description

`_triage_mark_infrastructure_retry` in `pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh:546` has no cooldown state — it logs the failure and returns immediately, with no mechanism to prevent the same issue from being evaluated again next cycle. When an issue has a permanent infrastructure failure (e.g., comment thread exceeds `_PAD_TRIAGE_MAX_COMMENT_BYTES=1048576`), the triage system re-evaluates it every cycle, re-downloads its comments, and re-logs the failure indefinitely.

Observed: issue #1419 in `<managed-repo>/netbox-wg` (294 comments, growing) triggers `github-comments-snapshot-too-large` **238 times** in a single session. Each occurrence downloads ~1MB+ of comment data, makes a `gh issue edit --remove-label triage-failed` API call, and logs — wasting API budget and log space every ~2 minutes.

## Expected Behavior

`_triage_mark_infrastructure_retry` should record the failure reason with a cooldown timestamp so the triage system skips the issue for at least N cycles (e.g., 30 minutes for `github-comments-snapshot-too-large`) before retrying. For permanent failures like oversized comment threads that cannot shrink, the backoff should escalate (e.g., exponential up to a day).

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `grep "github-comments-snapshot-too-large" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | wc -l`

**Actual output**: `238` in a single session (~8 hours)

**Expected output**: a small number (1-2 retries within an hour, then cooldown)

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:
- **Production entry point**: `pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh:863` -- `if [[ "$issue_comment_bytes" -gt "$_PAD_TRIAGE_MAX_COMMENT_BYTES" ]]`
- **Call chain**: `dispatch_triage_reviews` -> `_triage_dispatch_one` -> `_triage_fetch_issue_data` -> comment size check at line 863 -> `_triage_mark_infrastructure_retry "$issue_num" "$repo_slug" "github-comments-snapshot-too-large"` -> logs to LOGFILE, removes label, returns 0 — no state written
- **Integrated verification**: any issue with >1MB of comments will trigger this path every triage cycle indefinitely

**Causal code** (`pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh:546-555`):

```bash
_triage_mark_infrastructure_retry() {
    local issue_num="$1"
    local repo_slug="$2"
    local reason="$3"

    gh issue edit "$issue_num" --repo "$repo_slug" \
        --remove-label "triage-failed" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] Triage prefetch blocked for #${issue_num} in ${repo_slug} (reason=${reason}) — infrastructure failure, will retry without invoking the model" >>"$LOGFILE"
    return 0
    # ← NO cooldown state written
    # ← NO backoff tracking
    # ← message says "will retry" but retry is every cycle
}
```

There is no persistent state file or cache key that would prevent `_triage_dispatch_one` from re-selecting this issue next cycle. The triage dedup check (`_triage_is_cached`) only skips issues where a triage review was successfully posted — infrastructure failures never write to the triage cache, so the dedup never fires.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a managed issue with >1MB of comment content (e.g., 50+ verbose comments)
2. Run pulse for 1 hour
3. Count `github-comments-snapshot-too-large` in pulse.log

## Proposed Fix

Add a per-issue-per-reason cooldown state file (or entry in the existing triage cache) written by `_triage_mark_infrastructure_retry`. On subsequent calls, check the cooldown and return early without API calls or LOGFILE noise:

```bash
_triage_mark_infrastructure_retry() {
    local issue_num="$1"
    local repo_slug="$2"
    local reason="$3"
    local cooldown_seconds="${TRIAGE_INFRA_RETRY_COOLDOWN_SECONDS:-1800}"  # 30 min default

    # Check and set cooldown (in existing triage cache or separate state file)
    if _triage_infra_cooldown_active "$issue_num" "$repo_slug" "$reason"; then
        return 1  # silently skip
    fi
    _triage_infra_record_cooldown "$issue_num" "$repo_slug" "$reason" "$cooldown_seconds"

    gh issue edit "$issue_num" --repo "$repo_slug" \
        --remove-label "triage-failed" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] Triage prefetch blocked for #${issue_num} in ${repo_slug} (reason=${reason}) — infrastructure failure, cooldown=${cooldown_seconds}s" >>"$LOGFILE"
    return 0
}
```

For `github-comments-snapshot-too-large` specifically: since comment threads can only grow (not shrink), the cooldown could be much longer (e.g., 24h) or escalate exponentially.

## Workarounds Applied

None. The issue keeps being evaluated every cycle.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.201
- **Latest version**: 3.32.201
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

- `_PAD_TRIAGE_MAX_COMMENT_BYTES=1048576` (1MB limit, pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh:55)
- The "will retry without invoking the model" message is misleading — it retries immediately next cycle without any model call, which is correct, but there is no actual retry budget limiting
- Same pattern applies to other infrastructure failure reasons (scanner-unavailable, github-issue-body-malformed, etc.) — all share `_triage_mark_infrastructure_retry` with no cooldown
- Related session: GH#29024, GH#29043, GH#29046, GH#29053

title: bug(pulse-fast-fail): _ff_release_retry_reset_if_newer resets permanent data-issue failures on version upgrade — STALE_APPROVAL re-dispatched 44+ times after every aidevops update
body:
## Description

`_ff_release_retry_reset_if_newer_locked` in `pulse-fast-fail.sh:506` resets ALL fast-fail entries when the current aidevops version is newer than the version that recorded the failure — without checking the failure reason. This is correct for code bugs (a new version may have fixed the underlying issue), but incorrect for permanent data-issues like `permission_grant_unverified` (STALE_APPROVAL) or `no_work/stale_timeout` for inherently impossible issues.

Result: every aidevops version upgrade resets fast-fail backoff for issues whose block reason is unrelated to the code change, allowing them to be re-dispatched immediately and re-fail for 44+ cycles before the backoff kicks in again.

Observed: issue #3233 in `<managed-repo>` has reason `STALE_APPROVAL` (permission grant expired — a data problem, not a code bug). After upgrade from 3.32.198 to 3.32.201, the reset fired and the issue attempted dispatch 44+ times before fast-fail re-engaged.

## Expected Behavior

`_ff_release_retry_reset_if_newer_locked` should exclude failure reasons that are known-permanent data issues from the version-upgrade reset. At minimum, the following reasons should NOT be reset on version upgrade:
- `permission_grant_unverified` / `STALE_APPROVAL`
- `stale_timeout crash_type=no_work` (issue is inherently too hard/impossible)

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `grep "STALE_APPROVAL\|permission_grant_unverified" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | wc -l`

**Actual output**: `88` entries (44 dispatch attempts + 44 DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON entries) in session after upgrade

**Expected output**: `0` or `~4` (one check after upgrade to confirm still blocked, then cooldown)

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:
- **Production entry point**: `pulse-fast-fail.sh:861` -- `if _ff_release_retry_reset_if_newer ... ; then return 1; fi` called inside `fast_fail_is_blocked` (which is called by dispatch before each candidate)
- **Call chain**: dispatch evaluates issue #3233 -> `fast_fail_is_blocked` -> `_ff_release_retry_reset_if_newer` -> `_ff_version_gt current > failure_version` passes (3.32.201 > 3.32.198) -> `.count=0, .retry_after=0` written -> fast-fail no longer blocks -> dispatch proceeds -> `STALE_APPROVAL` block at dispatch-claim-helper -> rc=1 -> fast-fail re-records failure -> backoff starts again
- **Integrated verification**: trigger an aidevops upgrade while an issue has `permission_grant_unverified` failures; observe immediate re-dispatch attempts

**Causal code** (`pulse-fast-fail.sh:519-534`):

```bash
_ff_release_retry_reset_if_newer_locked() {
    ...
    _ff_version_gt "$current_version" "$failure_version" || return 1
    # ← resets count=0, retry_after=0 for ANY reason when version is newer
    # ← no check of .reason field
    # ← STALE_APPROVAL is a permanent data issue, not a code bug

    updated_state=$(printf '%s' "$state" | jq \
        '.[$k].count = 0 | .[$k].retry_after = 0 ...' 2>/dev/null)
    _ff_save "$updated_state"
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] fast_fail_release_retry_reset: ..." >>"$LOGFILE"
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Issue has `permission_grant_unverified` (STALE_APPROVAL) fast-fail entries
2. aidevops upgrades (version bumps)
3. Observe `fast_fail_release_retry_reset: #N ... reset stale failure from aidevops X.Y.Z` in pulse.log
4. Issue immediately re-enters dispatch loop and hits same block 40+ times

## Proposed Fix

In `_ff_release_retry_reset_if_newer_locked`, read the existing `.reason` field and skip the reset for known-permanent reasons:

```bash
_ff_release_retry_reset_if_newer_locked() {
    ...
    existing_reason=$(printf '%s' "$state" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '.[$k].reason // ""' ...)

    # Permanent data-issues: version upgrade cannot fix them
    case "$existing_reason" in
        permission_grant_unverified|stale_approval|STALE_APPROVAL)
            return 1 ;;  # do not reset
        stale_timeout|no_worker_process)
            # Only reset if not also crash_type=no_work (inherently impossible)
            local existing_crash_type
            existing_crash_type=$(printf '%s' "$state" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '.[$k].crash_type // ""' ...)
            [[ "$existing_crash_type" == "no_work" ]] && return 1 ;;
    esac

    _ff_version_gt "$current_version" "$failure_version" || return 1
    # ... rest of reset logic
}
```

## Workarounds Applied

None. After each upgrade, manually reset the fast-fail state is not practical.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.201
- **Latest version**: 3.32.201
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

- The reset mechanism is intentionally designed for code bugs — useful for `worker_launch_failed`, `no_worker_process` (launch code fixed), `rate_limit` (token rotated), etc.
- The design flaw: no distinction between "this failure was caused by the old code version" (should reset) vs "this failure is a data/config issue unrelated to code version" (should not reset)
- Affected reasons at minimum: `permission_grant_unverified`, `STALE_APPROVAL`, `no_work/stale_timeout` for issues that have had 10+ no_work cycles
- Related session: GH#29024, GH#29043, GH#29046, GH#29053

title: perf(release): collapse provenance tag scans before exact-tip snapshot
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `release aggregation publication timeout tag scan` → 0 hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: 3 recent commits / 0 related merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch the two target files.
- [x] File refs verified: both target files exist at current `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — release safety logic and fail-closed fallback behavior require judgment and regression tests.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped — the issue number is required before creating the safe implementation worktree.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-31
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session
- **Conversation context:** Repeated authorized release attempts for PR #29033 spent about 17 minutes scanning roughly 3,050 local semantic-version tags. Unrelated merges repeatedly advanced `main` before the helper created its exact-tip release checkout, so provenance correctly failed closed.

## What

Replace the per-tag subprocess loop in `_full_loop_release_find_tag_for_pr` with a one-pass, newest-first trailer index produced by `git for-each-ref`. Only tags whose parsed `Aidevops-Source-PR` or `Aidevops-Aggregated-Source` trailer can match the requested PR should enter the existing full source-JSON and signed-provenance verification path.

The optimization must preserve all fail-closed behavior: malformed matching trailers, text/JSON disagreement, invalid immutable source pairs, and failed Git enumeration must remain hard failures rather than becoming “not found.”

## Reproducer

On the current repository clone:

```bash
git tag --list 'v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*' | wc -l
# 3050

.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh patch 29033 incremental
```

The helper spent approximately 17 minutes in pre-snapshot tag discovery. It
started while reviewed aggregation PR #29052 was the exact `origin/main` tip at
`15731f9cac953c56bb7729b5e617b06aeb42fba0`, but only created its detached
release worktree after unrelated PR #29055 had advanced `main` to
`9bc2acb5dd5659e5d4b0ecfd597ec6cbaf45d0a9`. It then failed closed with:

```text
release-provenance: current main tip is not an explicit release-aggregation PR
```

The same race occurred on earlier reviewed aggregation tips. By contrast, one
`git for-each-ref` invocation with the trailer format below returns the complete
newest-first tag index in one process.

## Why

The current implementation invokes multiple Git/JQ subprocesses for every historical tag before snapshotting `origin/main`. With approximately 3,050 tags this takes long enough for normal repository traffic to invalidate the exact-tip release source. The resulting safe failures have already required several reviewed aggregation PRs and still prevent the explicitly authorized release from completing.

`git for-each-ref` already exposes trailer values in one process:

```text
%(refname:short)%1f%(trailers:key=Aidevops-Source-PR,valueonly,separator=%x2C)%1f%(trailers:key=Aidevops-Aggregated-Source,valueonly,separator=%x2C)
```

## Tier

- **Selected tier:** `tier:standard`
- **Rationale:** Two files change, but the production script is over 500 lines and release-provenance error handling must remain fail closed.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`

## Reference pattern

- Keep `_full_loop_release_find_tag_for_pr` responsible for reconstructing source JSON and invoking `_full_loop_release_verify_tag_provenance` on every candidate.
- Use `git for-each-ref --sort=-version:refname` only as a candidate prefilter; do not treat it as provenance verification.
- Use a non-whitespace field separator so absent source trailers do not shift aggregated-source fields under Bash 3.2.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tag enumeration runs through one `git for-each-ref` call rather than one body/parser subprocess chain per historical tag.
- [ ] Direct source and aggregated-source PRs match exactly; PR `89` must not match PR `890`.
- [ ] A matching malformed or inconsistent tag remains a hard failure.
- [ ] A failed `for-each-ref` command propagates as failure, not “no matching tag.”
- [ ] Candidate tags remain newest-first and still pass full signed provenance verification before reconciliation.
- [ ] Existing release reconciliation tests pass under Bash 3.2-compatible syntax.

## Verification

```bash
.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

After merge, retry the already-authorized PR #29033 patch release from a reviewed exact-tip aggregation and confirm the pre-snapshot guard completes before normal `main` traffic can invalidate it.

title: bug: init can commit on stale main and lose pre-push hook
body:
## Description

`aidevops init` can commit directly to a stale default branch, lose the
pre-push verification hook during Beads setup, report a critical security
posture, and still finish with `AI DevOps initialized!`.

This was observed with aidevops 3.32.201 on Ubuntu 24.04 using Bash 5.2.

## Expected behavior

- Before offering or accepting direct initialization on `main`, fetch and
  compare the local branch with its upstream.
- Refuse direct-main initialization when the branch is behind or diverged.
- Preserve and verify the aidevops pre-push hook after Beads hook installation.
- Distinguish local scaffolding success from incomplete remote hardening.
- Do not print an unconditional success result when required hook postconditions
  fail or the security posture is critical.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
aidevops init
```

1. Start with a clean local `main` that is behind `origin/main`.
2. Run `aidevops init`.
3. Choose `Continue on main`.
4. When Beads detects the existing pre-push hook, choose its recommended chain
   option.
5. Let initialization complete.

**Actual output**:

```text

Renamed pre-push to pre-push.old
Chained bd hooks with existing hooks
Git Hooks: Missing 1 recommended hook(s)
Git Upstream: Behind upstream by 4 commit(s)
Overall: CRITICAL
[OK] Committed initialized files
[OK] AI DevOps initialized!
```

The resulting local branch was ahead by one commit and behind by four. The
expected pre-push hook was missing.

**Expected output**:

Initialization should stop before writing or committing, explain that local
`main` is behind its upstream, and recommend a worktree based on the current
remote tip.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `aidevops-init-lib.sh:_init_validate_context`,
  entered by `aidevops init`.
- **Call chain**: `_init_validate_context` calls `check_protected_branch`; option
  2 returns success, then `_init_run_workflow` calls `_init_config_and_agents`,
  `_init_database_and_beads`, `_init_security_and_registration`,
  `_init_commit_files`, and `_init_print_summary`.
- **Integrated verification**: the production command created the local commit;
  `git rev-list --left-right --count main...origin/main` returned `1 4`, and the
  hook-status check reported the pre-push hook missing.

## Causal code

- `aidevops-init-lib.sh:_init_validate_context` calls
  `check_protected_branch` before writes.
- `aidevops-repos-lib.sh:check_protected_branch` checks only the branch name;
  option 2 returns success without checking upstream state.
- `aidevops-init-lib.sh:_init_config_and_agents` installs repo verification
  before `_init_database_and_beads` later runs `bd init`.
- No post-Beads hook integrity check verifies that the earlier pre-push hook
  survived.
- `_init_security_and_registration` treats a failed security assessment as a
  warning, while `_init_print_summary` always prints initialization success.
- `_init_commit_files` auto-commits the generated files even when upstream has
  diverged.

The missing upstream preflight and missing postcondition checks are confirmed.
The internal reason Beads reports successful chaining but leaves no pre-push
hook remains an integration-level investigation.

- Preserved the local initialization commit and generated files with the
  audited canonical mirror-recovery helper.
- Synchronized canonical `main` to the exact remote tip.
- Reinstalled the aidevops pre-push guards and wrapper/quality chain.
- Reapplied valid setup deltas through a linked worktree and pull request.
- Configured the missing GitHub workflows and branch protection separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- Direct-main initialization fails before writes when the default branch is
  behind or diverged.
- A regression test covers the interactive option-2 path with an upstream-ahead
  branch.
- A regression test runs the real repo-verify followed by Beads hook sequence
  and asserts the final pre-push chain is intact.
- Final output reports local initialization and remote hardening as separate
  states and never reports unconditional success after a required postcondition
  fails.

title: bug(pulse-nmr-reason.jq): false-positive 'billing' classification when no-work-escalation prose contains 'cost-circuit-breaker'
body:
## Description

`pulse-nmr-reason.jq` classifies a `needs-maintainer-review` episode as `billing/genuine-authority` on issues that received a `no-work-escalation-skip` comment. The comment's explanatory prose mentions `cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop` as documentation of what would happen if the no-work threshold were reached — but the JQ text-match filter fires on that string even though no circuit breaker was actually tripped. This produces a false `reason=billing` classification instead of the correct `diagnostic_ambiguity/temporary`.

Once the incorrect `<!-- nmr-decision-packet reason=billing -->` comment is posted, it becomes self-perpetuating: every subsequent cycle reads "billing" from its own prior comment, re-confirms the classification, and preserves NMR indefinitely. A valid `aidevops-signed-approval` (Case 2 in `auto_approve_maintainer_issues`) still clears the NMR label on the next cycle, but only because Case 2 runs after Case 1 is blocked — the NMR label stays on the issue longer than it should and the misleading log line `reason-coded NMR remains gated` is emitted on every cycle.

## Expected Behavior

An issue that received a `no-work-escalation-skip` comment (below the threshold that would actually trip the no-work circuit breaker) should be classified as `diagnostic_ambiguity/temporary`, not `billing/genuine-authority`. A valid cryptographic approval posted by the maintainer should clear NMR within one pulse cycle.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
grep "_nmr_applied_by_maintainer\|Skipping auto-approve" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep 3185
```

**Actual output**:
```
[pulse-wrapper] _nmr_applied_by_maintainer: #3185 in Majowka/mesh-manager — reason-coded NMR remains gated
[pulse-wrapper] Skipping auto-approve for #3185 in Majowka/mesh-manager — NMR manually applied by maintainer
```

**Verification that approval IS valid**:
```
$ bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh verify issue 3185 Majowka/mesh-manager
VERIFIED
```

**Root-cause JQ match confirmed**:
```
$ printf 'cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop marker that recognises' \
  | jq -Rs 'ascii_downcase | test("billing|cost-circuit-breaker|spend approval")'
true
```

**Priority order bug confirmed** (billing check wins over stale-recovery when both present):
```
$ printf 'cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop stale-recovery-tick:escalated' \
  | jq -Rs 'if (ascii_downcase | test("billing|cost-circuit-breaker")) then "billing-wins"
             elif (ascii_downcase | test("stale-recovery|worker_recovery_loop")) then "stale-wins"
             else "no-match" end'
"billing-wins"
```

**Expected output**: `"stale-wins"` — stale-recovery-tick:escalated is the actual NMR trigger, which should produce `diagnostic_ambiguity/temporary`.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `pulse-wrapper.sh` calls `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` calls `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` calls `_nmr_evaluate_reason_metadata` calls `_nmr_reason_metadata` calls `_nmr_reason_metadata_from_comments` calls `pulse-nmr-reason.jq`
- **Call chain**: `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` (pulse-nmr-approval.sh:1730) calls `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` (1122) which calls `_nmr_evaluate_reason_metadata` (1005) which calls `_nmr_reason_metadata` (886) which calls `_nmr_reason_metadata_from_comments` (876) passing ALL issue comments unfiltered to `pulse-nmr-reason.jq` via `jq -f`
- **Integrated verification**: Running `approval-helper.sh verify issue 3185 Majowka/mesh-manager` returns `VERIFIED` — the approval is valid — but the NMR label is not cleared by Case 1 due to this misclassification

**Causal code**:

```
# pulse-nmr-reason.jq — introduced in d4f84f6564 (2026-07-12)
# Line 11 — joins ALL comment bodies including ops:start blocks:
| ($comments | map(.body // "") | join("\n") | ascii_downcase) as $text

# Line 15 — fires on "cost-circuit-breaker" anywhere in text (including prose):
  elif ($text | test("billing|cost-circuit-breaker|spend approval"))
    then metadata("billing"; "genuine-authority"; "legacy-marker")

# Line 19 — correct match, but never reached when line 15 fires first:
  elif ($text | test("stale-recovery|worker_recovery_loop|diagnostic ambiguity"))
    then metadata("diagnostic_ambiguity"; "temporary"; "legacy-marker")
  # (intervening lines omitted for brevity)
```

```
# worker-lifecycle-common.sh:1366 — prose text containing sentinel string
# Introduced in commit 8009e50236 (2026-04-24)
# Posted inside <!-- ops:start ... ops:end --> but not excluded by JQ filter:
After ${nmr_threshold} consecutive `no_work` failures the per-issue no_work circuit
breaker (t2769) applies `needs-maintainer-review` with a `cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop`
marker that `_nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip` (t2386) recognises...
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A worker fails a `no_work` failure below the NMR threshold (e.g. 1 out of 3 required)
2. `escalate_issue_tier()` in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` posts the `no-work-escalation-skip` comment containing `cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop` in its body (line 1366), inside `<!-- ops:start ... ops:end -->`
3. The issue subsequently receives a `stale-recovery-tick:escalated` NMR via t2008
4. `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` runs, calls `_nmr_reason_metadata_from_comments` with all comments
5. `pulse-nmr-reason.jq` line 11 joins all comment bodies (including ops blocks) and lowercases
6. Line 15 fires on `cost-circuit-breaker` from the ops prose, classifying as `billing/genuine-authority/legacy-marker`
7. `_nmr_evaluate_reason_metadata` sets `_NMR_REASON_ACTION="preserve"` and posts `<!-- nmr-decision-packet reason=billing -->`
8. Every subsequent cycle: decision packet comment text now also contains "billing", re-confirming the same classification — self-perpetuating lock
9. Maintainer runs `aidevops approve issue N slug` — approval IS verified; Case 2 in `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` does eventually clear NMR, but Case 1 emits misleading `reason-coded NMR remains gated` on every cycle until then

## Workarounds Applied

- Maintainer ran `aidevops approve issue 3185 Majowka/mesh-manager` — posts a cryptographic approval which Case 2 in `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` correctly verifies (VERIFIED), allowing NMR to be cleared on the next cycle despite Case 1 being blocked

## Proposed Fix

**Fix 1 (required) — `pulse-nmr-reason.jq` line 11**: Exclude `<!-- ops:start ... ops:end -->` blocks from the joined text before pattern matching. These blocks are explicitly marked as audit trail, not implementation context:

```jq
# Before:
| ($comments | map(.body // "") | join("\n") | ascii_downcase) as $text

# After — strip ops blocks before joining:
| ($comments
   | map(.body // "" | gsub("(?s)<!--\\s*ops:start[^>]*-->.*?<!--\\s*ops:end\\s*-->"; ""))
   | join("\n") | ascii_downcase) as $text
```

Alternatively, filter out any comment whose body starts with `<!-- ops:start`:
```jq
| ($comments
   | map(select((.body // "") | startswith("<!-- ops:start") | not))
   | map(.body // "")
   | join("\n") | ascii_downcase) as $text
```

**Fix 2 (defense in depth) — `worker-lifecycle-common.sh:1366`**: Rephrase the prose to avoid embedding the sentinel string literally. Replace `cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop` with a non-matching description:

```bash
# Before:
...applies `needs-maintainer-review` with a `cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop` marker...

# After (avoids sentinel text in prose):
...applies `needs-maintainer-review` via the no_work breaker marker...
```

Fix 1 is the structural fix that makes the filter ops-block-aware. Fix 2 is hardening against future similar cases.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.201
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: 2.89.0

## Additional Context

Observed on Majowka/mesh-manager issue #3185. The `no-work-escalation-skip` comment was posted 2026-07-27T18:24:52Z; the stale-recovery NMR fired 2026-07-29T00:59Z. The `reason=billing` decision packet appeared 2026-07-31T21:30Z. The maintainer's signed approval was posted 2026-07-31T21:33Z and is VERIFIED — Case 2 will clear NMR at the next pulse cycle.

The self-perpetuating nature of the decision packet means that once this false positive fires, it cannot be auto-corrected by subsequent cycles — only the valid `aidevops-signed-approval` path (Case 2) breaks the loop. Any issue that received a `no-work-escalation-skip` comment and subsequently got stale-recovery NMR is potentially affected.

title: bug(triage): gate public review dispatch when required egress backend is unavailable
body:
## Problem

Public sandboxed triage requires a verified whole-process egress backend, but a normal deployment can enter the NMR queue with no `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_EGRESS_BACKEND` configured. Pulse then prepares each issue independently and launches a headless session that exits 126 before model execution. Infrastructure failures remain retryable, so this repeats without an actionable operator-level gate.

## Evidence

- Production runtime: aidevops v3.32.202.
- A targeted pass over #29019, #29020, #29021, and #29024 returned `aidevops.pulse-triage-outcome/v1` with `attempted=4`, `posted=0`, and `infrastructure_failed=4`.
- A controlled `headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role triage` diagnostic exited 126 with: `Whole-process worker egress is required but AIDEVOPS_WORKER_EGRESS_BACKEND is not an executable absolute path`.
- Synchronizing the clean canonical checkout fixed earlier immutable-evidence reads but did not change the runtime failure.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:318-330` forces `egress_mode=required` for public triage. `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh:951-1011` correctly fails closed when no backend is configured.
- #27056 / PR #27224 introduced the runtime-neutral backend contract and fail-closed semantics; this report is the missing deployment readiness, diagnosis, and queue-level backoff path rather than a request to weaken that boundary.

## Recommended scope

1. Add a deterministic backend readiness probe before per-item triage preparation or model launch.
2. Publish one typed cycle-level blocker when required egress is unavailable; do not launch every queued item only to receive exit 126.
3. Surface actionable operator guidance for configuring and probing `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_EGRESS_BACKEND`, while preserving required-mode fail-closed behavior.
4. Keep affected issues retryable after capability recovery, but bound repeated diagnostics and avoid consuming content retry budgets.
5. Add production-status/reporting coverage so Pulse health distinguishes `egress_backend_unavailable` from model/runtime failures.

## Files and patterns

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh` — gate `dispatch_triage_reviews()` once per pass and return a typed infrastructure outcome.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` and/or `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh` — expose a side-effect-free readiness probe using the existing v1 backend contract.
- EDIT: setup/status documentation path (exact owning file to confirm during discovery) — document provisioning and verification without bundling an unsafe pretend backend.
- EDIT: focused triage/runtime tests — prove zero model launches and one bounded diagnostic when the required backend is absent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing or invalid required egress backend is detected before any per-item headless launch.
- [ ] The triage outcome and Pulse health expose a controlled `egress_backend_unavailable` reason.
- [ ] No advisory comment or label is written and no content retry budget is consumed while capability is absent.
- [ ] A valid backend immediately restores normal review dispatch without manual issue mutation.
- [ ] Required public-triage containment remains fail closed; no environment override can silently downgrade it.
- [ ] Operator setup/status output explains the backend contract and probe command.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-network-egress.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-triage-output-shape.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-triage-security-gate.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh .agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --no-cache
```

title: Fail closed on mixed framed and unframed GH_DEBUG output
body:
## Problem

`gh-quota-debug-filter.py` suppresses recognized GH_DEBUG request ranges, but once any valid range exists it forwards every line outside those ranges. A malformed prefix or trailing fragment can therefore expose request headers or response payload data instead of failing closed.

## Evidence

- `.agents/scripts/gh-quota-debug-filter.py::_write_sanitized_stderr` emits every line whose index is outside `request_ranges`.
- The all-stream suppression guard applies only when no request range is recognized.
- This was identified during closeout review for #27777 and is pre-existing rather than introduced by that parser change.

## Scope

- Harden `.agents/scripts/gh-quota-debug-filter.py` so mixed framed/unframed GH_DEBUG content cannot disclose private payloads.
- Add focused regressions in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`.
- Preserve safe native diagnostics only through an explicit allowlist or another fail-closed mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A valid framed request followed by unframed private-looking content emits none of that private content.
- [ ] Unframed content before the first valid frame also remains suppressed.
- [ ] Malformed mixed streams retain exact attempt evidence where structurally provable and otherwise remain unknown; they never become synthetic zero-attempt captures.
- [ ] Existing safe-diagnostic behavior is either preserved through an explicit allowlist or intentionally narrowed with regression coverage.
- [ ] `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh` pass.
- [ ] `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` passes.

## Constraints

- Never print or persist raw authorization headers, query bodies, response bodies, or private telemetry.
- Do not relax quota exactness or malformed-frame fail-closed behavior.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh-quota-debug-filter.py` — `_write_sanitized_stderr` and request-range handling.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh` — GH_DEBUG privacy and framing fixtures.

title: Route internal PR check reads through exact-cost GraphQL
body:
## What

Replace framework-internal `gh pr checks --json` reads with a bounded helper that returns the required check fields and records each GraphQL page's operation-owned `rateLimit.cost`.

The helper must preserve the internal consumers' current check filtering, duplicate elimination, bucket mapping, JSON shape, and exit semantics while making quota attribution exact under concurrent GitHub activity.

## Why

A fresh post-deployment GH#27777 smoke recorded 27 structurally exact attempts but 3 unknown quota-cost attempts. All three came from native `gh pr checks`; two status-rollup pages consumed a counter delta of 2, and another overlapped concurrent account activity. Native GitHub CLI 2.96.0 performs finder, cached feature-detection, and paginated status-rollup requests, while its status query omits `rateLimit { cost }`. Counter deltas therefore cannot safely attribute the operation under concurrency.

Matched baseline/canary evidence remains blocked until the bounded smoke reports zero unknown quota/page attempts.

Ref #27777

## Pre-flight evidence

- Memory recall: no relevant stored lessons.
- Discovery: no open issue or PR matched `gh pr checks` exact-cost routing; related merged work includes #28646, #28775, #28817, #28909, and #29094.
- Installed dependency: `gh version 2.96.0`; upstream source and locally observed fields were checked before specifying compatibility behavior.
- Tier: `tier:standard` because this adapts an established operation-owned-cost pattern across several consumers and requires fallback/error handling.
- Seeded draft PR: skipped; the implementation should start from a fresh issue-linked worktree because `main` is moving rapidly.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh` — add the shared exact-cost PR-check JSON read.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` — route bounded check polling through the shared read.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` — route full-loop required-check evidence through the shared read.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh` — route CI-repair fallback collection through the shared read.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` — route the PR-level required-check fallback through the shared read.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/` — focused contract and integration coverage; choose existing test files where practical and add a dedicated test only when clearer.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-*pr-checks*`

### Complete Write Surface

- Callers/readers: the four native `gh pr checks` call sites above plus the shared wrapper loading path from `shared-constants.sh`.
- Mutation paths: none; all operations are read-only GitHub API calls.
- Tests/fixtures: check wait fixtures, full-loop remote-evidence tests, and Pulse required-check fallback tests.
- Schemas/config/generated mirrors: no persistent schema or migration. Deployment copies `.agents/scripts/` through the normal `setup.sh --non-interactive` path after merge; do not edit deployed runtime bundles directly.
- Rollback: revert consumers to native `gh pr checks`; no stored data migration is involved.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add one public shared helper that accepts repository, numeric PR, and required/all mode and emits the internal JSON superset: `name`, `state`, `bucket`, `link`, `workflow`, and any fields needed for duplicate elimination.
2. Resolve immutable PR identity and branch metadata through a bounded read, then query the status-check rollup by PR node ID. Include `rateLimit { cost }` in every GraphQL page and set `AIDEVOPS_GH_GRAPHQL_COST_FROM_RESPONSE=1` plus a stable `AIDEVOPS_GH_ROUTE_DECISION`.
3. Validate positive reported cost, GraphQL errors, node existence, commit/rollup presence, and cursor completeness before emitting data. Never infer a cost from account-counter deltas.
4. Match GitHub CLI 2.96.0 behavior used by current consumers: newest duplicate wins; required mode filters `isRequired`; CheckRun state uses conclusion only when completed; StatusContext uses its state; bucket mapping is `pass`, `skipping`, `fail`, `cancel`, or `pending`.
5. Preserve the current no-check/no-required-check diagnostics and `0`/`1`/`8` result contract expected by the wait, full-loop, and Pulse callers. API/parse/partial-page failures must remain indeterminate rather than becoming empty success.
6. Replace only framework-internal call sites. Do not intercept or reimplement the full user-facing `gh pr checks` CLI surface (`--watch`, templates, browser mode, arbitrary selectors).

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Concurrency: attribution must come from the same GraphQL response, not before/after account counters.
- Pagination: every page must carry its own reported cost; a missing cursor or partial connection fails closed.
- Required filtering: preserve `isRequired(pullRequestId: ...)`, including repositories whose required contexts are supplied by rulesets rather than classic branch protection.
- Duplicate runs: preserve newest-run selection keyed like GitHub CLI (status context name, or check name/workflow/event).
- Exit compatibility: cancelled, skipped, pending, and no-required-check cases need explicit regression fixtures because callers inspect both JSON and return code.
- Head drift: existing callers' exact-head checks remain authoritative; the new helper must not weaken them or cache mutable PR-number results.
- GitHub Enterprise compatibility: if the optional CheckRun event field is unsupported, use a tested fail-closed compatibility route rather than silently changing duplicate identity.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh .agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh`
- Run the focused new exact-cost helper test, including multipage and error fixtures.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`
- Deploy the merged code with `./setup.sh --non-interactive`, then run a bounded sanitized attribution smoke. Do not start matched baseline/canary collection unless unknown quota/page attempts are both zero.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every GraphQL status-rollup page used by internal PR-check reads supplies a validated operation-owned cost from that same response.
- [ ] Required/all filtering, newest-duplicate selection, field projection, bucket mapping, no-required diagnostics, and `0`/`1`/`8` outcomes match the current consumer contract.
- [ ] API errors, GraphQL partial data, missing commits/rollups, and incomplete pagination fail closed and never become `[]` success.
- [ ] All four framework-internal native `gh pr checks --json` paths use the shared exact-cost route.
- [ ] Focused tests, ShellCheck, and local lint pass.
- [ ] A post-deployment bounded smoke records zero unknown quota-cost attempts and zero unknown/unidentified/malformed pages before matched evidence collection resumes.

## Non-goals

- Replacing the user-facing GitHub CLI command globally.
- Assuming GraphQL cost is always 1.
- Publishing a release; merge/deployment and release authorization remain separate.
